To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the video streaming session suffers from starvation above a certain background load value and the load value at which the starvation occurs depends on the background traffic load characteristics.
there is an optimal load value for background traffic that maximizes the throughput of a unicast streaming video session.

the performance of streaming video over a wireless LAN depends on the background traffic and that there is a critical value for the background traffic load at which video streaming becomes starved of bandwidth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance evaluation of unicast streaming video over IEEE 80211 WLAN networks under varying background traffic loads.
the performance evaluation of video streaming over IEEE 80211 WLAN networks.
the performance evaluation of video streaming in the presence of background traffic in IEEE 802.1 networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a trade-off in the performance of the streaming application between the capacity of wireless network and the video quality.

the performance of video streaming over IEEE 802,11 WLAN networks depends on a combination of factors, such as the characteristics of the video stream, the characteristics of the wireless link and the characteristics of the traffic in the wireless network.

, for the case of a single source streaming a video to a single client over a single-hop IEEE 802. 11 WLAN, the performance of the video streaming application is not affected by the background traffic load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the background load has a significant impact on the video streaming performance.
the performance of a video streaming application in an IEEE 802.1l WLAN is very much dependant on the characteristics of background traffic.
, for a given video stream, there exists a maximum number of background traffic sources that the stream can tolerate without suffering a noticeable degradation in its quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of a streaming application is highly dependent on the background traffic load and that it is necessary to understand this relationship before deploying a streaming application over a wireless network.
background traffic can be detrimental to the performance of streaming video applications.
the background traffic load should be kept as low as possible in order to ensure that streaming sessions are able to achieve the desired quality of service (QoS) levels.
